citation.title: Explainable quantum neural networks for multi-material topology optimization
citation.authors: Dahyun Joo, Naruethep Sukulthanasorn, Kenjiro Terada, Do-Nyun Kim

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Against terminal MMA layouts, XQNN attained 81.4% to 94.0% material-type agreement on three validation load cases; the four-material predictions were less clean.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No end-to-end runtime or classical/ML time ratio is reported; Section 2.2 and Table S6 discuss only an early-stopping time/accuracy tradeoff.
claim.alternatives: Section 2.3 reports OOD, mesh-transfer and 3D material accuracy and normalized compliance against terminal MMA; Table S6 qualitatively notes an early-stopping acceleration benefit.

baseline.classical_method: Section 4.1: MMA-based multi-material topology optimization with FE equilibrium and compliance minimization.
baseline.implementation: Section 4.1: adapted from Zheng et al.'s MATLAB two- and three-dimensional MMTO code.
baseline.hardware_ml: Section 4.3: AMD Ryzen 7 9700X 8-Core Processor for exact Qiskit statevector simulation.
baseline.problem_size: Sections 2.2-2.3: training/validation/OOD 50 x 25 elements; transfer 100 x 50, 150 x 75, 200 x 100 elements; 3D 20 x 20 x 10 voxels.
baseline.classical_iterations: Section 4.1: terminal MMA stops at grayscale ratio <0.02 for regular 2D/3D and <0.01 for high-resolution 2D; iteration counts not stated.
baseline.quality_metric: Sections 2.2-2.3: material-type accuracy and normalized compliance Cpred/CGT; Table S2 gives material-volume constraints.
baseline.quality_gap: Section 2.2: validation accuracy 81.4%-94.0%; Section 2.3: 3D mean accuracy 89.3%, 79.6%, 73.6% and mean normalized compliance 0.96, 0.98, 0.83 for two, three, four materials.

R1.evidence: Section 2.2: primary quantitative comparison is design agreement with terminal MMA, not a measured speed comparison.

R2.evidence: Sections 4.1-4.3: MMA implementation and ML CPU are identified, but no same-task times, per-iteration times or hardware contrast establish an R2 criterion.

R3.evidence: Section 2.2 and Table S6 claim an early-stopping acceleration benefit without training or data-generation costs or a break-even calculation.

R4.evidence: Section 2.3 and Figures S6-S8 report compliance of predicted layouts [inferred FE verification]; Section 2.3 notes disconnected members and no enforced volume constraints, but gives neither violation magnitudes nor failure rates.

reporting.n_test_cases: Section 2 and Table S1: O1-O4 = 4 OOD conditions, HR1-HR3 = 3 resolution cases, 3D1-3D4 = 4 three-dimensional conditions, each at 2/3/4 materials; V1-V3 = 3 validation conditions.

notes: Section 2.3 reports some predictions stiffer than terminal MMA but explicitly says XQNN does not enforce volume constraints. The primary comparison is quality; the paper gives only qualitative acceleration discussion, with no observed end-to-end speed-up. Sections 5-6 offer data and code on request.
